subject: Many covariance matrices of varying size

messages.author: ba46e0c634632e6f
messages.subject: Many covariance matrices of varying size
parts: I have a model were I need to define many covariance matrices, but these covariance matrices are of varying sizes. For example, if I have n_i observations for each of N subjects, then I need to define something like cov_matrix[n_i] c_i for each N subjects. Is this possible to do in Stan so that I might be able to index them for each subject in the model code? From what I can tell in the documentation, and what I've found in this users group, it's not clear to me if this is possible except in the case where the n_i are the same for all N subjects.

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Many covariance matrices of varying size
parts:
On 11/16/12 5:48 PM, Ryan wrote:
> I have a model were I need to define many covariance matrices, but these covariance matrices are of varying sizes. For
> example, if I have n_i observations for each of N subjects, then I need to define something like cov_matrix[n_i] c_i for
> each N subjects. Is this possible to do in Stan so that I might be able to index them for each subject in the model
> code? From what I can tell in the documentation, and what I've found in this users group, it's not clear to me if this
> is possible except in the case where the n_i are the same for all N subjects.

I'm afraid it's not possible. All the
variable declarations are rectangular.

It's not even easy to hack it the way you can
for the ordinal example from a few days ago
because the covariance matrix structure is
more complex (it could be done, but you'd need
to parameterize your own Cholesky factor then
do a lot of index fiddling to put things back
together again).

For a given fixed data set, it's possible to
explode out the model and index everything by
size. But if there are lots of different values
for n_i[n], then that gets ugly.

We've been considering adding some ragged
data structures along the following lines:

int<lower=0> N; // number of subjects
int<lower=1> n_obs[N]; // num observations for subject n in 1:N
cov_matrix[n_obs] c; // cov matrices for subject n in 1:N

The intent of the notation is that c[n] for n in 1:N
is an (n_obs[n] x n_obs[n]) covariance matrix.

This notation lets us do a single final layer of
raggedness and could apply anywhere there's a size. So

real y[n_obs];

could be used for the observations themselves. y[n]
would be a size n_obs[n] array.

It's not something we're going to add right away
because of all the I/O and connections to R would
have to be upgraded.

- Bob
